claims.text: The 5.00 SGD fee cannot stand, because POL-NS-23 makes it conditional on the driver having performed two acts before cancelling for no-show: at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call. The trip record's own derived contact check reports call_count 0, an empty in_app_calls array, and obligation_met false. The second limb of a conjunctive obligation failed, so the fee is voided and no driver compensation is payable.

The alternative route to compliance in POL-NS-23 - a voice-call entry in the chat log - is also empty. The chat log contains exactly two entries, both IN_APP text messages sent by the driver (MSG-05062-001 at 10:17:20 and MSG-05062-002 at 10:20:45), and nothing in the nature of a voice call. Neither limb of POL-NS-23's contact requirement is satisfied on this record.

The driver's own account - that he 'messaged and called the passenger two times' - is contradicted by the platform record on the very element that decides the case: the only two contacts on file are messages, and the in-app call count is zero. His application therefore rests on an assertion the record falsifies, and the rider's statement that he never called her is the account the evidence supports.

The missing call was not for want of opportunity. The driver-device trace shows the vehicle at the pickup and stationary from 10:16:41 to 10:23:11 - every fix in that stretch reports 0 kph - and the code-computed arrival check places the nearest fix 5.75 m from the pickup at 10:17:11 with 4 m reported accuracy, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so arrival is corroborated. The driver had more than six stationary minutes at the door in which a single in-app call could have been placed.

The fee does not turn on the free wait. Even assuming POL-NS-21's 300-second wait was properly served - arrival recorded at 10:17:00, cancellation at 10:23:30, 390 seconds later - POL-NS-23's contact obligation stands as a separate precondition of the same fee, and time served at the kerb cannot cure a call that was never made.

With the fee voided, the driver is owed nothing and the state the ledger already records should stand: the fare breakdown shows payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00, following the fee_reversed event at 11:56:30, so the rider is not carrying the disputed charge. The filing party is the driver and his claim is not supported, so the ruling is NO_ACTION - which is party-relative and never means restoring a charge - with neither amount field populated.

The rider's recollection that she only saw the messages after the cancellation is not the ground of this case and need not be accepted: the chat log's read receipts show both messages delivered and read before the 10:23:30 cancellation (10:17:33 and 10:21:22). That does not assist the driver, because a message, read or unread, is not a call, and POL-NS-23 demands both.

Nothing adverse should attach to the rider's account on this trip. The rider profile snapshot carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, and POL-NS-25 applies only where that optional field is present and stands at 3 or more, so no repeat no-show referral can fire; and since the fee does not stand, this trip cannot be counted toward such a flag in any event.

A conjunctive obligation with one limb missing fails, so the fee is voided and no driver compensation is payable. Time served at the kerb cannot cure a call that was never made.

ledger.claim: The 5.00 SGD fee cannot stand, because POL-NS-23 makes it conditional on the driver having performed two acts before cancelling for no-show: at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call. The trip record's own derived contact check reports call_count 0, an empty in_app_calls array, and obligation_met false. The second limb of a conjunctive obligation failed, so the fee is voided and no driver compensation is payable.

The alternative route to compliance in POL-NS-23 - a voice-call entry in the chat log - is also empty. The chat log contains exactly two entries, both IN_APP text messages sent by the driver (MSG-05062-001 at 10:17:20 and MSG-05062-002 at 10:20:45), and nothing in the nature of a voice call. Neither limb of POL-NS-23's contact requirement is satisfied on this record.

The driver's own account - that he 'messaged and called the passenger two times' - is contradicted by the platform record on the very element that decides the case: the only two contacts on file are messages, and the in-app call count is zero. His application therefore rests on an assertion the record falsifies, and the rider's statement that he never called her is the account the evidence supports.

The missing call was not for want of opportunity. The driver-device trace shows the vehicle at the pickup and stationary from 10:16:41 to 10:23:11 - every fix in that stretch reports 0 kph - and the code-computed arrival check places the nearest fix 5.75 m from the pickup at 10:17:11 with 4 m reported accuracy, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so arrival is corroborated. The driver had more than six stationary minutes at the door in which a single in-app call could have been placed.

The fee does not turn on the free wait. Even assuming POL-NS-21's 300-second wait was properly served - arrival recorded at 10:17:00, cancellation at 10:23:30, 390 seconds later - POL-NS-23's contact obligation stands as a separate precondition of the same fee, and time served at the kerb cannot cure a call that was never made.

With the fee voided, the driver is owed nothing and the state the ledger already records should stand: the fare breakdown shows payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 5.00, following the fee_reversed event at 11:56:30, so the rider is not carrying the disputed charge. The filing party is the driver and his claim is not supported, so the ruling is NO_ACTION - which is party-relative and never means restoring a charge - with neither amount field populated.

The rider's recollection that she only saw the messages after the cancellation is not the ground of this case and need not be accepted: the chat log's read receipts show both messages delivered and read before the 10:23:30 cancellation (10:17:33 and 10:21:22). That does not assist the driver, because a message, read or unread, is not a call, and POL-NS-23 demands both.

Nothing adverse should attach to the rider's account on this trip. The rider profile snapshot carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter, and POL-NS-25 applies only where that optional field is present and stands at 3 or more, so no repeat no-show referral can fire; and since the fee does not stand, this trip cannot be counted toward such a flag in any event.

The free-wait element of this charge is made out under POL-NS-21. This was an on-demand trip, so the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival: he marked arrival at 10:17:00, the wait expired at 10:22:00, and he cancelled at 10:23:30 — 390 seconds after arrival — so the cancellation fell after the free wait expired and not before it.

The arrival is corroborated by the trace and is not merely a button-press. The driver-device GPS trace's nearest fix sits 5.75 m from the pickup at 10:17:11 and reports a horizontal accuracy of 4 m — inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — so the trace's own arrival_check returns corroborated true and the POL-NS-21 arrival test is satisfied.

The amount carried on the record is exactly the policy amount. The fare breakdown shows a cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD and a total charged of 5.00 SGD, and fee_matches_policy is true against the 5.00 SGD policy fee; where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00, that being the money moved to the driver for his time and fuel and not a second payment.

The rider's account is demonstrably wrong where it can be checked. His statement that he 'only saw his messages after he cancelled' is contradicted by the chat log's own delivery and read records: MSG-05062-001 was read at 10:17:33 and MSG-05062-002 at 10:21:22, both well before the 10:23:30 cancellation. The rider therefore had the driver's messages in front of him during the wait, and his denial of the calls is the assertion of a party shown to be unreliable on the contact chronology.

No profile entry can decide this trip. POL-GEN-01 confines profile evidence to fraud_flags and no_show_cancellations_30d and makes every other entry context only: the driver's fraud_flags is 0 and the rider's profile carries no fraud flag, so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar is not engaged, and no other entry on either profile — the driver's no_show_terminations_30d of 3 included — may establish a fact about this trip or ground its outcome.

I do not overstate the second limb of POL-NS-23. That clause requires at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call before cancellation, and it fixes where the call must appear — trip_record.in_app_calls, or a voice-call entry in the chat log. trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, the chat log holds two text messages and no voice-call entry, and the derived contact_before_cancel records call_count 0 and obligation_met false. The driver's filing asserts two calls, but no artifact corroborates one, and the rule voids the fee where either limb is missing. The driver's claim to the 5.00 SGD therefore cannot be sustained: with the fee voided and 5.00 SGD already refunded (payment_status REFUNDED; fee_reversed at 11:56:30), DRIVER_COMPENSATION is not available to him, and the read-off under POL-GEN-03 is NO_ACTION, which leaves the refund to the rider standing.
